python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Convertible foreign currencies (in millions of dollars) for CY 1963-1977
data = {
    1963: 212,
    1964: 432,
    1965: 781,
    1966: 1321,
    1967: 2345,
    1968: 3528,
    1969: 2781,
    1970: 629,
    1971: 276,
    1972: 241,
    1973: 8,
    1974: 5,
    1975: 80,
    1976: 320,
    1977: 18
}

values = list(data.values())
print("Data points:", values)
print("Count (n):", len(values))

# Calculate mean
mean = sum(values) / len(values)
print(f"Mean: {mean}")

# Calculate sample standard deviation
# Using formula: s = sqrt(Σ(xi - x̄)² / (n-1))
variance = sum((x - mean) ** 2 for x in values) / (len(values) - 1)
std_dev = math.sqrt(variance)
print(f"Sample standard deviation: {std_dev}")

# Fisher-Pearson adjusted skewness coefficient
# g1 = (n / ((n-1)*(n-2))) * Σ((xi - x̄) / s)³
n = len(values)
numerator = sum(((x - mean) / std_dev) ** 3 for x in values)
denominator = (n - 1) * (n - 2)
g1 = (n * numerator) / denominator

print(f"Fisher-Pearson adjusted skewness: {g1}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {round(g1, 3)}")
EOF

import math

# From treasury_bulletin_1970_12_page_94.txt and treasury_bulletin_1978_12_page_91.txt
values = [212, 432, 781, 1321, 2345, 3528, 2781, 629, 276, 241, 8, 5, 80, 320, 18]

print(f"n = {n}")

# Calculate mean
mean = sum(values) / n
print(f"Mean: {mean}")

# Calculate sample standard deviation (using n-1 in denominator)
variance = sum((x - mean) ** 2 for x in values) / (n - 1)
std_dev = math.sqrt(variance)
print(f"Sample std dev: {std_dev}")

# Calculate Fisher-Pearson adjusted skewness
# Formula: g1 = (n / ((n-1)*(n-2))) * Σ((xi - x̄)/s)³
# This is the bias-corrected sample skewness

# First calculate the sum of cubed z-scores
sum_cubed_z = sum(((x - mean) / std_dev) ** 3 for x in values)
print(f"Sum of cubed z-scores: {sum_cubed_z}")

g1 = (n / ((n - 1) * (n - 2))) * sum_cubed_z
print(f"Fisher-Pearson adjusted skewness: {g1}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {round(g1, 3)}")
EOF
